name: JetBrains AI Assistant
description: AI features embedded in JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm, etc.). The open IDE project is the workspace unit; AI chat history is stored per-project in IDE workspace files. JetBrains Junie (2025, GA June 2026) adds an agentic coding agent that plans and executes multi-step tasks within the project file scope.

identity_and_auth.user_identity_model: Account-based via JetBrains Account (OAuth) plus a JetBrains AI subscription. Alternatives: Bring Your Own Key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, OpenRouter, GitHub Copilot), authorizing integrated coding agents with their own provider accounts (e.g., sign in with a ChatGPT account to use the OpenAI Codex agent; a Claude Agent powered by Anthropic's Agent SDK is included in the JetBrains AI subscription), or pointing at local runtimes (Ollama, LM Studio, LiteLLM) so code never leaves the machine. Logout is via Settings | Tools | AI Assistant | Providers & API keys. The underlying IDE itself can be used with a normal JetBrains license; the AI layer adds the AI subscription / key requirement.
identity_and_auth.multi_user_collaboration: No shared AI workspace at the consumer level — AI Assistant is per-developer, scoped to the local IDE installation and the open project. Team/org capabilities come through JetBrains IDE Services (AI Enterprise): centralized admin controls, SSO, profile-based policies, model/provider access governance, execution-permission policies, audit logging, on-premises LLM hosting, and adoption/usage analytics. Junie guidelines provide a shared team context layer via version-controlled project files rather than a live shared session. There is no documented real-time multi-user co-editing of a single AI chat thread. [uncertain] Whether AI chat threads themselves can be shared between team members.

workspace_model.workspace_definition: The workspace unit is the JetBrains IDE project (the file scope of the currently open project). It maps to a directory/repo on disk that the IDE has opened. AI context, chat history, and Junie agent scope are all framed around this open project. Per-installation IDE metadata (including AI chat) is stored in workspace XML files under the JetBrains config dir (e.g., ~/.config/JetBrains/<IDE><version>/workspace). The project is a real filesystem/repo entity rather than a virtual cloud object.
workspace_model.workspace_session_binding: AI chat sessions are intended to be scoped to the active project/workspace; chat data is stored in per-project workspace XML files. A user can maintain multiple named chats ('All Chats' list) and switch between them via the Chat History button (rename/delete supported). Junie tasks run within the open project and can run asynchronously, staying available from anywhere the user signs in (remote monitoring). Known caveats: chat history is unavailable in Remote Development (issue LLM-19392, though chats persist in the workspace XML), 'New Chat' has no confirmation so active chats can be accidentally lost, and history can be lost during IDE upgrades (LLM-12257). [uncertain] Whether multiple concurrent active chat sessions can run simultaneously vs. one active at a time.
workspace_model.context_scoping: Context is project/workspace-scoped by default: the open project's files supply code context, chat history lives in that project's workspace files, and Junie guidelines/skills load at project level. Global/account-level: provider/model configuration, BYOK credentials, and global Junie guidelines (~/.junie/AGENTS.md) and user-level agent skills. Session-level: the individual chat thread / Junie task plan and action log. .aiignore (project-level) excludes sensitive paths from AI context. Junie respects .aiignore and will not process listed files unless explicitly permitted.
workspace_model.config_file_instruction_precedence: Junie guidelines provide persistent reusable project context, added to every task. IDE-plugin lookup order: (1) custom path set in Settings | Tools | Junie | Project Settings; (2) .junie/AGENTS.md (preferred standard location); (3) AGENTS.md in project root. Junie CLI lookup order: (1) custom file via JUNIE_GUIDELINES_FILENAME; (2) .junie/AGENTS.md; (3) AGENTS.md (root); (4) .junie/rules/*.md (all markdown concatenated); (5) .junie/guidelines.md (legacy, still supported; legacy .junie/guidelines/ folder also). Global guidelines: ~/.junie/AGENTS.md (Windows %USERPROFILE%\.junie\AGENTS.md) apply across all projects. Conflict resolution: if both global and project guidelines exist, both are included and marked, and PROJECT-LEVEL ALWAYS TAKES PRECEDENCE over global. CLI config.json has project-level (team-shared, in repo) and user-level (personal machine defaults) tiers resolved highest-priority-first. Guidelines are plain Markdown. [uncertain] Documented max file-size cap for guidelines files.
workspace_model.source_corpus_grounding_scope: Not a source-corpus / research-notebook product. Grounding is the open project's codebase, augmented by Junie guidelines, agent skills (.junie/skills/ at user and project levels, invoked only when relevant to a task), and MCP servers. There is no bounded document-set abstraction (no NotebookLM-style notebook or Perplexity Space).

persistence_and_history.persistence_mechanism: Local-first. AI chat history and IDE session state are persisted in per-project/per-installation workspace XML files on disk under the JetBrains config directory (e.g., ./config/JetBrains/<IDE><version>/workspace or ~/.config/JetBrains/<IDE><version>/workspace). Junie project context lives in version-controllable files under .junie/ in the repo. Provider credentials are stored locally via the IDE's credential store. No mandatory cloud DB for the user's chat history — model traffic goes to the chosen LLM provider but transcripts are not persisted cloud-side by default (zero data retention with third-party providers for text inputs; optional opt-in JetBrains telemetry retained <=30 days internally only).
persistence_and_history.session_history: Chats are organized in an 'All Chats' list, browsable via the Chat History button, where the active chat can be renamed or deleted. Stored as structured entries inside the workspace XML files (effectively per-project). Retrieval is via the chat panel UI. Reliability caveats: not surfaced in Remote Development (LLM-19392), can be wiped on IDE upgrade (LLM-12257), and 'New Chat' silently starts a fresh thread with no confirm. A marketplace plugin ('AI Assistant Providers / Sessions') adds a Session Browser and exposes AI session data via IntelliJ's built-in MCP server so any MCP client can search/retrieve past coding sessions. [uncertain] Native export/portability format for chat history beyond raw workspace XML.
persistence_and_history.memory_layering: Layered: (a) durable user-authored project context = Junie guidelines (.junie/AGENTS.md, applied to every task) and agent skills (loaded only when task-relevant); (b) global personal/org rules = ~/.junie/AGENTS.md; (c) ephemeral per-session state = the individual chat thread / Junie task plan + action log. Junie documents a 'guidelines and memory' concept where guidelines are the persistent reusable layer. [uncertain] Whether there is an automatically-generated, self-updating long-term memory store (akin to Windsurf/Claude auto-memory) distinct from user-authored guidelines.
persistence_and_history.search_retrieval_history: Natively: browse the 'All Chats' list per project; no prominently documented full-text/semantic cross-project search in the core product. The third-party 'AI Assistant Providers / Sessions' plugin adds searchable session retrieval exposed through the IDE's MCP server, enabling cross-session search/retrieval by MCP clients. Cross-project recall otherwise relies on shared guidelines files rather than searching old chats.
persistence_and_history.lifecycle_ttl_cleanup: Chat history persists on disk with the project's workspace files until manually deleted or until it is lost through known failure modes (IDE upgrade resetting the All Chats list; not accessible in Remote Dev). No TTL/expiration on local history is documented. Optional opt-in JetBrains telemetry (full LLM communication, off by default, Settings | Data Sharing | Send detailed code-related data) is retained internally for <=30 days max and never shared externally; zero data retention applies to third-party provider text inputs. [uncertain] Whether old/inactive chats are ever auto-archived or pruned.

execution_and_isolation.sandbox_isolation_model: Two modes. (1) AI Assistant chat / inline edits run in-process within the IDE against the open project (no separate sandbox; edits applied to real project files with user review). (2) Junie agent execution: runs locally by default, but tasks can run inside Docker containers and Git worktrees for sandboxed, parallel work, with JetBrains Air managing reintegration of changes into the main codebase. JetBrains is also testing cloud execution where agents run in isolated remote sandboxes (enterprise offering in progress). Junie can run terminal commands, run tests, use MCP servers, and (GA feature) drive the IDE debugger (set breakpoints, step, inspect variables) against live runtime. .aiignore bounds what files the agent may touch.
execution_and_isolation.snapshot_state_restore: Git worktrees provide effective per-task filesystem isolation/restore points for Junie's sandboxed runs. Environment reproducibility for containerized runs comes via Docker. [uncertain] Whether there is a first-class, named snapshot-and-restore of machine/env state (installed packages, env vars) independent of git, comparable to Devin snapshots; the documented primitives are Docker containers + git worktrees rather than a saved environment image feature.
execution_and_isolation.cloud_local_handoff: Junie runs locally by default and asynchronously, and the session stays available 'from anywhere you sign in' with remote monitoring of long-running tasks. Junie CLI is a standalone agent that runs in the terminal, in any IDE, in CI/CD, and on GitHub/GitLab, enabling continuity across surfaces. Cloud execution in isolated remote sandboxes is in testing. Local-only / on-prem operation (local models, on-premises LLM via AI Enterprise) is fully supported. [uncertain] Degree of live state preservation when moving a single in-progress session between local and cloud.
execution_and_isolation.parallelism_subagent_fanout: Junie supports parallel sandboxed work via Git worktrees + Docker containers, with Air coordinating merge-back into the main codebase. Junie CLI supports custom subagents. So beyond single-session chat, there is a coordinator-style pattern for parallel agent tasks isolated per worktree/container. [uncertain] Documented hard limit on the number of concurrent parallel Junie agents.
execution_and_isolation.trigger_surface: IDE (AI Chat panel, inline actions, Junie agent inside the JetBrains IDE plugin); standalone Junie CLI (terminal, any IDE, CI/CD pipelines, GitHub/GitLab). Async long-running tasks with remote monitoring. Enterprise governance through IDE Services. [uncertain] First-class Slack or chat-ops trigger surface.

implementation.implementation_stack: Client: JetBrains IDE platform (IntelliJ Platform) with the AI Assistant plugin and Junie plugin. Local persistence: per-project/per-installation workspace XML files (under the JetBrains config dir) for chat history and session state; local credential store for BYOK/provider keys; .junie/ directory in the repo for version-controlled guidelines (AGENTS.md / rules/*.md / legacy guidelines.md), agent skills (.junie/skills/), and CLI config.json (project + user tiers). Models: JetBrains AI subscription routing plus BYOK (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, OpenRouter, GitHub Copilot) and local runtimes (Ollama, LM Studio, LiteLLM, OpenAI-compatible servers). Integrated agents: OpenAI Codex (ChatGPT login), Claude Agent (Anthropic Agent SDK). Junie execution: local, Docker containers, Git worktrees, with Air for reintegration; cloud isolated sandboxes in testing. MCP: IDE has a built-in MCP server; Junie consumes external MCP servers. Enterprise: IDE Services (SSO, profiles/policies, audit logging, on-prem LLM, analytics). The 'AI Assistant Providers / Sessions' marketplace plugin layers a Session Browser + MCP-exposed session search and multi-account quota tracking. [uncertain] Exact serialization schema of the workspace XML chat entries.
implementation.applicability_to_labmate: JetBrains AI Assistant is a strong reference for project-scoped session storage with a layered, version-controlled context model. Mappings for Labmate: (1) workspace == the open project (a real repo/dir); Labmate's workspace_id should likewise scope chat/session history so threads don't leak across workspaces (the Zed-style cross-project leakage and JetBrains' workspace-XML scoping both argue for strict workspace_id partitioning of Labmate's MongoDB session docs). (2) Two-tier persistence parallels Labmate well: durable, user-authored project context (Junie .junie/AGENTS.md guidelines + skills) ~ Labmate's long-term MongoDB session/instruction docs; ephemeral active task state (the chat thread / Junie task plan) ~ Labmate's Redis Streams active-session state with TTL and LangGraph thread_id checkpointing (each Junie task plan/action log is analogous to a LangGraph thread). (3) Config precedence is a directly reusable design: project-level overrides global, custom-path > standard file > root file, with both included-and-marked on conflict — Labmate can adopt the same project>global cascade for instructions. (4) Junie's per-task git-worktree/Docker isolation maps to giving each Labmate agent run an isolated checkpoint/branch so parallel runs don't corrupt shared workspace state. (5) Identity: JetBrains Account + BYOK/local-model options show a tiered identity model; Labmate's Discord connector is the session entry point and the Discord user id is the natural durable-memory key, analogous to the JetBrains Account keying AI access. (6) Reliability lesson: JetBrains' history loss on upgrade and missing confirm-on-new-chat are anti-patterns — Labmate should make session creation explicit and migration-safe.
